data.title: Meta's Muse Passes ChatGPT to Become No. 1 App in U.S. App Store
data.description:
Muse AI, the new AI agent from social media giant Meta Platforms (META), has reached the top of Apple's (AAPL) U.S. App Store just over one week after its launch. Muse now ranks number one overall, ahead of AI developer OpenAI's ChatGPT at number two. In addition, Google's (GOOGL) Gemini ranks eighth, while Anthropic's Claude sits at number 13. The strong start gives Meta an important win as it tries to compete with other companies that already have millions of people using their AI assistants.

One reason Muse stands out is that it can do more than answer questions. For example, Muse can send emails or book trips. It can also open a web browser and fill out forms. Meta says it can even negotiate for users in certain situations.

The process starts when a user gives Muse a goal. From there, the app can create a personalized plan and organize the steps needed to complete it. Muse can then continue the work on its own, even after the user closes the app. If a task requires permission, Muse can stop and ask the user before taking the next step.

Muse Is Already Ahead of Several Major AI Rivals

Importantly, the App Store rankings show how quickly Muse has caught people's attention. Space and AI company SpaceX's (SPCX) Grok currently ranks 32nd, while software giant Microsoft's (MSFT) Copilot sits much lower at 64. This means that Muse has already moved ahead of several well-known AI products despite launching only recently.

Meta Chief AI Officer Alexander Wang celebrated this achievement on X and said that the company has been excited to see what people are already doing with Muse.

The early success also gives Meta a new way to put its AI directly in front of consumers. Until now, much of Meta's AI strategy has been dependent on apps such as Facebook and Instagram. Muse is different because it is a standalone product that competes directly with ChatGPT and Gemini.

data.title: Intel Stock (NASDAQ:INTC) Slips Despite SK Hynix Response on Intel Deal
data.description:
What a difference two days makes. We only recently heard about a possible deal brewing between chip stock Intel (INTC) and chip maker SK Hynix (SKHY). But SK Hynix recently responded to that deal, noting that there was no deal at all between the two. Or at least, no deal has been established yet, which is in line with the reports we heard from two days ago. Investors were disheartened, though, and gave Intel stock a nearly 2% loss in Friday afternoon's trading. Intel has seen a 267.82% rally in its share price over the past year.

No Deal, Yet

SK Hynix, a report from Techzine noted, has denied that any plans are confirmed. This is reasonable enough, as the reports that there even were plans at all emerged just two days ago. The statement that SK Hynix released noted that it was "…exploring various options to strengthen its global competitiveness."

This is reasonable enough, and given that the early word around the plans focused on the Ohio plant—which has still not been built just yet—the idea that the plans would take a while to coalesce, let alone start, was not out of line. The Ohio plant was originally supposed to start production this year, but new reports push that back to 2030.

Promotion

AutoSR to Hit Panther Lake Chips

Meanwhile, the Panther Lake lineup is set to get a bit of a boost. Microsoft (MSFT) will be offering support for the Automatic Super Resolution (AutoSR) function on Panther Lake. AutoSR is a comparatively new system, released back in 2024, and allows systems access to resolution upscaling where it was not available before.

Results with AutoSR have been impressive, though. Using Assassin's Creed: Valhalla as a benchmark, testing done at TechPowerUp got 1600p resolution with "High" in-game settings got the frame rate increased from 45 FPS to 52 FPS. AutoSR hopes to get that number to 60, which will certainly be helpful for games and other applications that support no other form of upscaling.

data.title: Coinbase Stock (COIN) Soars 12% as Baird Says SEC Exemption Puts Offerings 'More on Par' with Robinhood's
data.description:
Shares in U.S. crypto exchange Coinbase (COIN) continued their rally on Friday afternoon, jumping 12% to around $194. This came as crypto stocks rallied following a new exemption from the U.S. securities watchdog. The new policy now allows trading in tokenized U.S. stocks. COIN also jumped after Robert W. Baird analyst Robert Bamberger noted that the exemption puts Coinbase's asset-class offerings "more on par" with those of brokerage Robinhood (HOOD).

Baird Says SEC Exemption Is 'a Positive' for Coinbase

On Wednesday, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) issued the "Innovation Exemption." The exemption allows platforms to trade certain tokenized U.S. stocks on blockchains for five years.

The agency said the goal is to enable innovation while it considers broader regulation for on-chain trading. Paul Atkins, SEC's chair, noted that the exemption will help to "bring America's capital markets into the digital age."

In response, Bamberger noted that the exemption is "a positive for Coinbase, particularly with CLARITY Act delays." On September 15, the U.S. Senate failed to advance the key crypto legislation. This came as the Act failed to secure the required number of votes to move forward.

Why Baird Remains on the Sidelines on Coinbase Stock

Despite the bullish comments, Bamberger maintained his Hold rating on Coinbase shares. He also kept his price target at $130, representing about 34% downside.

Yet, the analyst noted that he is more positive on Coinbase than before. This is due to three factors:

  • Coinbase is seeing a rebound in volume. In other words, more people are trading on the crypto exchange's platform
  • Regulatory trends affecting the industry are becoming more favorable
  • Coinbase continues to develop its "Everything Exchange" strategy. Under the strategy, the exchange is expanding beyond crypto trading.

Is Coinbase a Good Stock to Buy?

data.title: U.S. Automakers Call on Trump to Maintain Ban on Chinese Vehicles: GM, F, STLA
data.description:
The U.S. automotive industry is calling on U.S. President Donald Trump to maintain policies that make it difficult for Chinese automakers to operate in and sell their vehicles within the American market. In a letter to Trump, lobby groups representing major U.S. automakers such as General Motors (GM), Ford (F), and Stellantis (STLA) urged the president to "maintain policies that keep the door firmly shut to Chinese automakers seeking to sell, import or manufacture vehicles inside the U.S."

"The automotive sector is foundational to our advanced manufacturing and defense base, with the capacity and workforce to respond during a national emergency. Once that base is hollowed out, it can't be rebuilt overnight," reads the letter. Currently, the U.S. imposes a steep 100% tariff on Chinese electric vehicle imports and heavy duties on other Chinese auto imports to protect domestic manufacturing.

The steep tariffs have meant that Chinese autos are effectively barred from the U.S. market.

data.title: California Governor Gavin Newsom Signs Executive Order to Rein in AI Companies: NVDA, AAPL, GOOGL
data.description:
California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed an executive order aimed at addressing the potential dangers related to artificial intelligence (AI). The executive order is potentially consequential as many leading technology companies such as Nvidia (NVDA), Apple (AAPL), and Google parent company Alphabet (GOOGL) are headquartered in California's Silicon Valley.

Newsom is among the 2028 Democratic presidential candidates that are urging a more aggressive regulatory approach to rapidly evolving AI technologies, which has alarmed voters. But Congress appears unlikely to take any meaningful legislative action on AI fears right now and U.S. President Donald Trump has resisted calls for regulations, labeling the concerns a "hoax."

Gavin Newsom's Executive Order

"The federal government's abject failure to create any form of meaningful AI oversight or accountability should alarm every American, especially when AI CEOs themselves are begging for regulation," said Newsom in a news release. "We're not waiting to act – we're going to speed up our work on substantial and responsible AI oversight before it's too late."

Promotion

NVDS: built for a short position on NVDA

The California governor's executive order calls on a group of experts to meet and create, within two months, a guide for the state to strengthen its AI safety and security laws. Those enhanced laws may include a requirement for independent third parties to write safety plans for frontier AI companies, and/or mandate that companies develop a "kill switch" to shutdown their models in case of emergency.

Newsom, whose term as California governor ends on Jan. 4 of next year, has not formerly announced a presidential campaign, though he has said he is considering the possibility and political pundits expect him to run for the White House.

data.title: Boeing Stock (NYSE:BA) Ticks Up as Starliner Comes Back
data.description:
The Starliner program was a fairly big black eye to aerospace stock Boeing (BA). The debacle that followed, in which two astronauts were left on the International Space Station for around nine months instead of the original nine days it was expected to be, weighs on Boeing to this very day. But Starliner may be getting a new lease on life soon. This caught investors' interest, and Boeing stock ticked up fractionally in Friday afternoon's trading. Boeing has seen a 8.65% loss in its share price over the past year.

Winner By Default

Apparently, SpaceX (SPCX) is planning to wind down the Crew Dragon program. Given that the Crew Dragon saved the last Starliner mission and got Boeing's astronauts home safely, this leaves the whole space program without a reliable spacecraft. Thus, NASA is putting some extra work in to get the Starliner up and running, according to a report from Ars Technica.

NASA will be ordering another two crewed missions as early as next week, the report noted. Further, NASA will foot the bit for fixing the thruster issues and will even offer support to get launch duties squared away. SpaceX, the report noted, wants to focus on the Starship rocket and getting more Starlink satellites in orbit.

Lufthansa Steps Up Its Purchases

Boeing also landed some good news from The Lufthansa Group (DLAKY), who agreed to pick up more Boeing 737 MAX aircraft. Reports noted that Lufthansa had some additional options in reserve for purchase, and decided to exercise those options, picking up another 20 737 MAX 10 aircraft. The options came after Lufthansa agreed to pickup 40 737 MAX 8 aircraft back in 2023. The new MAX 10s, meanwhile, will not be delivered until the early 2030s.

data.title: Joby Aircraft Flies 3,199 Miles Across America With Zero Pilot Inputs
data.description:
Air taxi developer Joby Aviation (JOBY) has completed what it says was the first fully autonomous flight across the United States. Indeed, a converted Cessna Caravan equipped with Joby's technology traveled 3,199 miles from Concord, California, to North Carolina's Outer Banks with zero control inputs from the onboard safety pilot. The aircraft handled taxiing and takeoff on its own. It also navigated the route and completed its landings autonomously under remote supervision.

This is important because the flight tested the system in real-world conditions rather than on a short demonstration route.

During the trip, the aircraft crossed busy airspace and high-altitude terrain. It also adjusted its route around severe weather. Remote teams supervised the aircraft from Joby's California autonomy headquarters and Shaw Air Force Base in South Carolina. At one point, the flight was being supervised from as far as 2,323 miles away.

Promotion

Joby CEO JoeBen Bevirt said the journey offers a look at what autonomous aviation could eventually become.

Joby Is Building Autonomy for More Than Air Taxis

It is worth noting that the aircraft used for the trip was not Joby's electric air taxi. Instead, Joby installed its autonomous technology on a Cessna Caravan, which shows that the system could potentially work on different types of aircraft.

That creates opportunities outside passenger transportation. For example, Joby has suggested that autonomous cargo flights and emergency response could be potential use cases. The company is also testing defense logistics. Before the cross-country milestone, Joby said that the platform had already completed more than 400 flights and over 800 hours of automated flight time.

The stock initially moved higher after the announcement before giving up those gains. Joby shares remain down sharply this year as investors continue to weigh the large amount of spending needed to develop autonomous aircraft and the regulatory approvals required before fully autonomous commercial flights can become common.
